Clicking the plain "Suchen" button with all filters left empty returned all rows unfiltered - only 10 total, i.e. this appears to be NRW's small, complete list of Grundwasserkörper (groundwater bodies), so no filter is actually needed to get the full dataset. Opened the first result row's Objektdetails page, which offers 17 sub-view tabs (Stammdaten, Programmmaßnahmen, Belastungsfaktoren, Bewirtschaftungsziele, Schutzwirkung, Landnutzung, Bodenart, Bodentyp, Hydrogeochemische Einheiten, Hintergrundwerte, Oberirdische Einzugsgebiete, Grundwasserabhängige Landökosysteme, Profilschnitt, Wasserschutzgebiete, Zustandsbewertung, Veröffentlichte Daten zum BWP, Risikobewertung) - none named "Lage", and no "Ostwert"/"Nordwert" strings found in the result-table header, the result-table first row, or the default (Stammdaten) detail-page text. Grundwasserkörper are area/polygon features (groundwater bodies), not point features, so they plausibly have no simple point coordinate fields at all - any spatial geometry is likely only available via a map/WMS layer or the "Profilschnitt" (cross-section) view, not as tabular Ostwert/Nordwert values. No Excel-export button was checked in this pass (out of scope for recon), but given only ~10 rows an export/full scrape would be trivial either way. Two consecutive runs were consistent (opened_ok, row_count=10, search_type, coordinate findings all matched); a transient race condition once caused discover_search_fields to report 0 selects instead of 7 on one run, likely due to the advanced-search panel still AJAX-rendering - re-running resolved it, worth a short settle-wait if scripting this dataset for real later.

name: Bauwerke (Querbauwerke)
search_form_notes: Standard regional-search widget present (input id ends with gemeindeName_idCommon2, "BR/Kreis/Gemeinde"), confirming this dataset follows the shared ELWAS-WEB search pattern. Search form (inside mainDataIframe) also exposes 3 plain <select> filters (Zuständige Behörde, Bauwerksart [Fischaufstieg/Querbauwerk/sonstiges Bauwerk/Wasserkraftanlage], Bauwerkstyp) and 13 text inputs incl. numeric Ostwert/Nordwert range fields and Absturzhöhe von/bis - i.e. the list-result search form itself lets users filter by coordinate range, but the RESULT TABLE columns (checked via thead) do not surface Ostwert/Nordwert as columns. Filled regional search with "Düren" and submitted -> 10 result rows returned, well within the ui-datatable-data table (no Excel-export button noticed in this pass, not specifically checked). Opened the first result row's detail page: no sub-view tab dropdown appeared (get_detail_tab_options returned []), but Ostwert/Nordwert values were found directly on the base Stammdaten detail page text. One operational note: on a cold session, the mainDataIframe's search form (selects/inputs/Suchen button) sometimes had not finished rendering by the time discover_search_fields() ran immediately after open_dataset() (0 selects/0-1 inputs found on 2 successive attempts); adding an explicit wait_for("input[value='Suchen'], select", state="attached", timeout=8000) after get_frame() before inspecting the form resolved this and gave two consecutive matching results (kreis_regional / row_count=10 / has_coordinates=true / detail_stammdaten). This iframe-render race is worth carrying into any real scraper for this and other ELWAS datasets.

name: Versorgungsgebiete
search_form_notes: This dataset does NOT use the standard Kreis/Gemeinde 'gemeindeName_idCommon2' regional-search widget - no such field is present. Instead the search form has: teisIdNr (plain text, TEIS-ID des Versorgungsgebietes), vgNameID (autocomplete, Versorgungsgebiet-Name), gesundheitsamtID (autocomplete, zustaendiges Gesundheitsamt), wasservorgungsanlageID (autocomplete, Wasserversorgungsanlage), and berichtsjahr (plain text input, reporting year - e.g. '2022'). No <select> elements exist on the search form at all. Clicking 'Suchen' with everything blank returns 0 rows (confirmed) - Berichtsjahr is effectively a required filter. Filling berichtsjahr='2022' and submitting returned 10 rows (one results page; pagination controls present so the true total for that year is likely larger, not sampled further per single-recon-pass scope). Result list columns: TEIS-ID des Versorgungsgebietes, Bezeichnung, Wasserversorgungsanlage(n) die das VG beliefert, Zustaendiges Gesundheitsamt - no Ostwert/Nordwert columns. Opened the first detail row (EN_Herdecke): Objektdetails page has 3 sub-tabs (Stammdaten / WVA mit PNS WW-Ausgang / Netzprobenahmestellen Untersuchungsergebnisse), no 'Lage' tab. Checked all three tabs' full inner text - none contain 'Ostwert' or 'Nordwert'. Stammdaten only shows TEIS-ID, ZID, Versorgungsgebiet name, Wasservolumen [m3/d], Berichtsjahr. Conclusion: Versorgungsgebiete (water-supply-area polygons) appear to be an attribute-only dataset in this UI with no point coordinates exposed anywhere in list or detail views; the polygon geometry (if published) is presumably only available via a separate WMS/geodata service, not through this search/detail interface. For AquaRevier integration this dataset would need to be joined by Gemeinde/area name or Gesundheitsamt rather than by lat/lon, and any bulk pull would require iterating berichtsjahr values (and possibly paginating) since no unfiltered 'export everything' path exists.

name: Messstellen Chemie und Biologie (Auswertung)
search_form_notes: This dataset is NOT the standard single-step search+list pattern used by the other 4 integrated ELWAS datasets - it is a two-stage 'Auswertungen' (report) builder. STAGE 1 ('Vorauswahl' panel, AJAX-rendered ~1-2s after page load - discover_search_fields found 0 selects if queried too early, 2 selects once settled): two required <select> fields, no gemeindeName_idCommon2 and no input[value='Suchen'] present yet. Select 1 id=...preSelectPanel:fachbereich_Row:fachbereichId options=[Biologie, Chemie]. Select 2 id=...preSelectPanel:auswOptRow:auswOpt options=[Stammdaten ausgewählter Messstellen, Fundort Taxon, Artenliste, Biologie Bewertung Messstelle, ACP Bewertung] - this picks which REPORT TYPE to generate. Submitted via input[value='Start'] (not 'Suchen'). STAGE 2 (after picking first options Biologie + Stammdaten ausgewählter Messstellen and clicking Start): a full search panel appears containing the standard gemeindeName_idCommon2 regional-search widget PLUS Gewässername/OFWK(3D/3E)/SeeWK(3D/3E)/Messnetz filters and a Messstellennummer field - but the results table (tbody.ui-datatable-data, get_result_row_count works) is already pre-populated with ALL 4883 matching Messstellen with no filter applied, so no regional search was actually needed to get rows. Result table thead columns are only Messstellennummer | Messstellenname | Gewässername - no Ostwert/Nordwert substrings anywhere in the header. Row count (4883) is far above the cheap-sampling threshold, and the one detail-row click I attempted anyway (ec.open_detail_row) timed out after 30s waiting for a clickable row link/submit-input - this table looks like a checkbox-driven multi-select 'assemble your report' table (row selection for building an export) rather than the per-row Objektdetails-link table used elsewhere in ELWAS, so the standard open_detail_row/get_detail_tab_options/Lage-tab coordinate check does not apply cleanly here and I could not confirm coordinates that way. A real scraper for this dataset would need to: (1) handle the Vorauswahl step (5x2=10 Fachbereich/Auswertungstyp combinations, each is a different report shape/columns), (2) figure out the actual row-selection/export mechanism (checkboxes + a generate/export action, not a simple detail link) on stage 2, and (3) separately check whether an Excel-export button exists on stage 2 (not checked here) as that would avoid the row-selection question entirely per the toolkit's stated best practice.

name: Maßnahmenprogramm

Selecting the first Bewirtschaftungsplan option ("BWP 2022-2027") and resubmitting returned 10 rows - confirmed on 2 separate runs (row count came through reliably even though the actual Playwright .click() call itself twice reported a 30s/10s timeout, apparently because the AJAX search response replaced/detached the "Suchen" button under the locator mid-click - the search itself did complete both times).
